locations: Kroo Bay | Falcon Bridge
summary: September 2007 rainy-season flooding in Sierra Leone (ReliefWeb GLIDE FL-2007-000177-SLE); an IRIN photo caption dates Kroo Bay flooding to September 2007, and the same IRIN article mentions a separate 2007 flood at Falcon Bridge where a resident died trapped under a boulder (that incident's month is not given). Weakly sourced; day unknown.
evidence: ReliefWeb disaster page title: "Sierra Leone: Floods - Sep 2007"; IRIN (2008) says 2007 flooding at Falcon Bridge left a resident "trapped for hours under a boulder" (search-result paraphrase)

time_of_day: night of Thu 11 Sep into Fri 12 Sep (overnight storm; ~5 hours of torrential rain)
locations: Kroo Bay | Freetown (several parts)
rain_note: About five hours of torrential rain; Met official called it the heaviest daily rainfall of the year, but the rain gauge was broken so there is no measurement
summary: An overnight storm flooded parts of Freetown under more than 1 m of water and tore down dozens of makeshift homes in Kroo Bay, affecting more than 10,000 slum dwellers (government evaluation of 15 Sep); a mission blog reported ten deaths in Kroo Bay (not officially confirmed) and AFP noted unconfirmed reports of people buried by boulders.
evidence: "More than 10,000 slum dwellers have been affected by an 11 September storm that tore down dozens of makeshift homes in Kroo Bay" (IRIN); "submerged in more than 1m of water on Friday after five hours of torrential rain" (M&G, 12 Sep 2008)

locations: Freetown
rain_note: Part of about two weeks of heavy rainfall in August 2009
summary: Late-August 2009 flooding in Freetown left four dead according to the government (IRIN); cumulative August 2009 totals for Freetown were 15 dead and 425 displaced (UN-SPIDER/Wikipedia), which probably include the 13 Aug landslide; exact day not found.
evidence: IRIN: flooding "in the capital Freetown in late August left four dead, according to the government"; Wikipedia: "two weeks of heavy rainfall in August, left 15 deaths and 425 displaced in Freetown"

locations: Freetown (three hillside houses; neighbourhood not named)
rain_note: Heavy rain (no amount reported)
summary: A rain-triggered landslide collapsed three hillside houses in Freetown on Thursday 13 Aug 2009, killing at least 7 and injuring 15 sleeping residents, while flooding left at least 300 people homeless (landslide-tagged).
evidence: "at least seven people were killed and 15 injured when homes collapsed in a landslide in heavy rain in Sierra Leone's capital Freetown on Thursday" ... "Flooding has left at least 300 people homeless" (Reuters)

locations: Owen Street
rain_note: Torrential overnight rain that also blocked roads across the city (no amount reported)
summary: A pre-dawn mudslide after torrential rain brought down houses on a hill slope at Owen Street, Freetown, killing 16 (police via AFP; State House/Cocorioko said 13, mostly children) with 5 more in critical condition.
evidence: "Sixteen people were killed in a mudslide that swept away their homes in Sierra Leone's capital Freetown on Monday following torrential rains, police said" (AFP)

locations: Gray Bush | east and west of Freetown
rain_note: Torrential rain; first downpour of the rainy season (no amount reported)
summary: Torrential rain on Sunday 4 May 2014 dislodged a huge boulder that crushed a house in Gray Bush, killing 5 according to Reuters (4 according to AFP), while overflowing streams and gutters damaged houses and roads in the east and west of Freetown (rockfall/landslide-tagged).
evidence: "three men and a young girl died in the Sierra Leone capital, Freetown, after torrential rains on Sunday dislodged a huge boulder which then crashed into a house" (AFP); "Five people, including two children, were killed on Sunday" (Reuters)

locations: Freetown
rain_note: Torrential rains in the first and second weeks of September 2015; no amounts reported
summary: Torrential rain in the first half of September 2015 reportedly caused flood damage in and around Freetown before the major 16 September flood; exact days, places and impacts were not found and the reports may partly overlap the 16 September event.
evidence: Torrential rains in the first and second weeks of September 2015 caused extensive damage in and around Freetown, Sierra Leone, largely due to rivers bursting their banks.

locations: Kroo Bay | Krootown Road | Culvert | Moyiba | Aberdeen | Cockerill Bay | Wilkinson Road | Wilberforce | Signal Hill | Lumley
rain_note: Continuous heavy rain over the preceding couple of days; one report describes a six-hour torrential downpour on 16 Sept; no amounts reported
summary: Torrential rain on Wednesday 16 Sept 2015 flooded low-lying settlements across Freetown; reported deaths ranged from 4 (State House) to 12 (VOA), with 10 the figure most often cited later; 12,000-14,000 people were affected and about 3,000 sheltered in the National (Siaka Stevens) and Attouga stadiums; the government ordered people to stay home on 17 Sept.
evidence: At least four people were killed and scores injured following torrential rains in Sierra Leone's capital on Wednesday (Reuters); later summaries: 14,000 people affected and 10 reported dead.

time_of_day: early morning (Regent/Sugar Loaf slope collapse reported at about 05:45); heavy rain on 13-14 Aug
locations: Regent | Sugar Loaf | Babadorie River Valley | Kamayama | Malama | Juba | Juba Bridge | Kaningo | Lumley | Culvert | Dwazark | Mountain Cut | George Brook | Gbangbayilla | Wellington
rain_note: Three days of torrential rain beforehand; about 1,040 mm in Freetown from 1 Jul to 14 Aug (about 3x normal); >100 mm in the 7 days to 12 Aug (Weather Underground); one study cites three consecutive days with 126 mm, 10-14 Aug
summary: After three days of torrential rain, part of Sugar Loaf mountain collapsed above Regent in the early morning, sending a debris flow about 6 km down the Babadorie/Juba river valley to Lumley while flash floods hit other parts of Freetown; about 500 bodies were confirmed and 1,141 dead or missing is the most-cited total, with more than 3,000 left homeless (landslide plus floods).
evidence: Sugar Loaf mountain partially collapsed, triggering mudslides in the early morning of August 14, which damaged or completely submerged several houses and structures; at least 3,000 people are homeless and over 300 houses have been destroyed.

locations: downtown Freetown | Kroo Bay
rain_note: Extremely heavy rain over central and western Freetown that night; no amount reported
summary: New overnight flooding in downtown Freetown, 12 days after the Regent disaster, flooded the Kroo Bay health centre, bridge and school; 1 person died and 2 were injured.
evidence: New flooding appeared on the night between Saturday and Sunday 26/27 August in downtown Freetown, and has flooded a health centre, the bridge and a school at Kroo Bay. One person is reported dead and two injured.

time_of_day: overnight: heavy continuous rain from about 22:00 on 1 Aug until the morning of Friday 2 Aug
locations: Kroo Bay | Culvert | Bathurst | Blackhall (Kissy) | Cline Town | Queen Elizabeth II Quay | Moeba | Kuntholoh | Bololo | Temne
rain_note: Heavy continuous downpour from 22:00 on 1 Aug to the next morning; came after persistent torrential rains since late May 2019 on saturated soil; no amounts reported
summary: Overnight torrential rain caused flash floods and landslides across Freetown and Western Rural: 7 bodies were confirmed (1 Kroo Bay, 2 Culvert, 3 Bathurst after a wall fell on a house), the perimeter wall of the Queen Elizabeth II Quay was breached and people were trapped in Blackhall, Kissy; ONS counted 985 households completely damaged and 5,381 people homeless (5,000-8,000 displaced in other estimates).
evidence: At least seven people are dead after flash flooding hit Freetown on Friday 2nd August, 2019 amid torrential rains, mortuary sources said.

locations: Freetown
summary: A second flood hit 14 Freetown communities (not named) in the early hours of 15 Aug 2019; a quick assessment found 200 more households affected, almost a third of them completely destroyed.
evidence: in the early hours of August 15th, more flooding was reported in 14 communities in Freetown, and 200 more households were affected, with almost one-third of these completely destroyed.

locations: Freetown lowlands and floodplains (no neighbourhoods named)
rain_note: Heavy rain; on 15 July 2020 Freetown City Council warned of heavy rain forecast for three more days
summary: Flooding on 14 July 2020 displaced residents of low-lying and floodplain areas of Freetown (the Sierra Leone Telegraph described minor displacement), prompting a Freetown City Council flood warning the next day.
evidence: ACAPS (4 Aug 2020): flooding on 14 July 2020 "has displaced residents living in lowlands and floodplains"; needs "currently unclear".

locations: Portee | Rokupa
summary: Flooding of the coastal slums of Portee and Rokupa in eastern Freetown left about 60 people homeless and one dead (figures from Politico-SL 2020 as cited in peer-reviewed studies; flood mechanism not specified).
evidence: "the flooding left about 60 people homeless and resulted in one fatality (Politico-SL, 2020)"

locations: low-lying areas of Freetown (no neighbourhoods named)
rain_note: Heavy rains during the week ending 30 July 2021
summary: During the week ending 30 July 2021 heavy rains flooded low-lying Freetown communities with water several feet deep, and many people lost their homes (exact day not given).
evidence: "Communities in low-lying areas of Freetown are once again at the receiving end of the heavy rains... many people have this week lost their homes, as floods reaching several feet destroy houses and livelihoods" (Sierra Leone Telegraph, 30 Jul 2021)

locations: Culvert | Kroo Bay
rain_note: Heavy downpour on 17 Aug; Caritas describes flooding from 14 to 17 Aug 2022; first of two heavy rain spells in two weeks
summary: A heavy downpour on 17 August 2022 flooded Culvert and Kroo Bay; Caritas Freetown said Culvert was worst hit in flooding between 14 and 17 August.
evidence: "Culvert and Kroo Bay were flooded after a heavy downpour on 17 August, 2022"; Caritas: Culvert "was the worst hit in the flooding from August 14 to 17"

locations: Looking Town | Kissy | Colbert | Culvert | Kroo Bay | Kaningo | Tengbeh Town | Kanikay | Cassava town | Brooks field
rain_note: Torrential rain on Sunday 28 Aug (Caritas: flooding 27-28 Aug); second heavy spell in two weeks; major roads 'transformed to heavy flowing rivers'
summary: Torrential rain on Sunday 28 August 2022 caused flash floods and a mudslide at Looking Town (Kissy) that killed six; AFP/Red Cross counted 8 dead (79 injured, 4 missing), NDMA said 800+ were displaced in Colbert, and the Red Cross DREF counted 12,903 people (1,817 households) affected by the late-August floods.
evidence: "At least eight people have been killed and hundreds displaced" (AFP); Telegraph: "six, including a family of three, were killed after a mudslide destroyed two homes in an informal settlement" at Looking Town

locations: Cline Town | Moyeiba | Kissy (Leone Oil facility) | PWD Junction, Pademba Road | Campbell Street
rain_note: Storm with heavy rain 9-10 May 2023
summary: A storm with heavy rain on 9-10 May 2023 caused floods and mudslides in Freetown, killing at least 7 (six in a wall collapse at Cline Town, one in a mudslide at Moyeiba); NDMA reported flood damage at the Leone Oil facility in Kissy and the PWD Junction on Pademba Road flooded.
evidence: "At least 7 people have lost their lives after storms and heavy rain caused flooding and mudslides in parts of Freetown." (FloodList)

locations: Freetown (no neighbourhoods named)
rain_note: Heavy rains, August 2023
summary: NDMA's national disaster risk management policy records severe flooding in Freetown and other parts of the country from heavy rains in August 2023, affecting over 10,000 people nationally (day and Freetown-only figures not given).
evidence: NDMA policy: in August 2023 "heavy rains led to severe flooding in Freetown and other parts of the country, affecting over 10,000 people"

locations: Congo Town | Kolloh Town | Gray Bush
rain_note: Persistent rains in Freetown since 1 July 2024
summary: In early July 2024 (before NDMA's 8 July assessment) flooding affected 200 households in Congo Town, Kolloh Town and Gray Bush, and a slope collapse in Congo Town killed one person and brought down a house.
evidence: NDMA: flooding "affected 200 households in Congo Town, Kolloh Town, and Gray Bush"; "a slope collapse in Congo Town resulted in one death and the collapse of a house"

locations: Waterloo | East End of Freetown | Allen Town-Waterloo Highway
rain_note: 59.2 mm cumulative rainfall 16-17 July 2024 (SLMet)
summary: Flooding hit Waterloo and other East End communities on 16-17 July 2024 after 59.2 mm of rain; a school fence collapsed on the Allen Town-Waterloo Highway and one woman was briefly hospitalised (NDMA/SLMet joint assessment on 17 July).
evidence: flooding "linked to a significant cumulative rainfall of 59.2mm recorded from July 16-17, 2024"

locations: Freetown low-lying areas | Connaught Hospital | SS Camp | Haja Soni Drive, Mortomeh
rain_note: 106 mm in 3 hours (09:00-12:00) at SLMet Tower Hill station on Saturday 20 July 2024; highest since rains began 1 July; several days of rain
summary: Extreme rain on Saturday 20 July 2024 (106 mm in three hours) flooded low-lying Freetown; during the same multi-day spell Connaught Hospital wards were submerged, and a five-storey building at SS Camp collapsed late on 21 July amid heavy rain (reports of 1-2 dead, several missing).
evidence: SLMet "recorded a cumulative rainfall of 106mm from 9:00am to 12:00 noon"; Telegraph (24 Jul): "The wards in Freetown's main hospital were submerged in water after several days of rain"

locations: Texaco, Old Road | Upper Melon Street, Old Road | Lower Kuntolor
rain_note: Intense rain on 24 October 2024
summary: Intense rain on 24 October 2024 caused severe flooding: a fence collapse at Upper Melon Street (Old Road) swept away two men (one found dead, one missing), a school and church compound flooded at Texaco Old Road, and eight mud-brick homes were destroyed at Lower Kuntolor, displacing 150+ people (30 households).
evidence: NDMA: at Lower Kuntolor "eight mud-brick homes were destroyed by runoff from hillside waterways, displacing more than 150 people across 30 households"

locations: New England Ville (54 Off Pratt Street) | central Freetown
rain_note: Heavy downpour on the evening of Wednesday 23 July 2025
summary: A heavy downpour on the evening of 23 July 2025 sent floodwater and mud from the hills through New England Ville, collapsing a compound fence and destroying a home; NDMA confirmed three dead and a one-year-old girl missing, and floodwater also halted the President's motorcade in central Freetown.
evidence: NDMA: "at approximately 6:00 PM, following a heavy downpour, a section of a compound fence collapsed due to the massive flow of floodwater and mud cascading from the surrounding hilltops"

locations: Susan's Bay
rain_note: Heavy morning rain
summary: Heavy morning rain on 23 May 2026 made a blocked, waste-filled gutter overflow into homes and pathways at Susan's Bay; no casualties were immediately reported.
evidence: Sierraloaded: gutter overflowed into homes; "No casualties were immediately reported at the time of reporting."

time_of_day: overnight into the early hours of Monday 3 August (6-7 hours of rain)
locations: Juba | Portor | Metchem | Femi Turner Drive | Mama Wurie (Femi Turner) | Goderich
rain_note: Nearly seven hours of heavy rain (Truth Media); about six consecutive hours of exceptionally heavy rainfall on the night of 3 August (IFRC)
summary: Six to seven hours of heavy rain on 3 August 2026 caused flash floods and slope collapses across Freetown: a wall collapse at Metchem killed a girl, her mother and grandmother, more than 300 homes flooded in Juba/Portor with two children missing, and IFRC counted 4 dead, 8,915 people (1,763 families) affected, 700+ houses damaged or flooded and 18 water sources contaminated (DREF MDRSL022).
evidence: In Juba "over 300 homes were 'completely flooded'" (NDMA via Sierra Leone Telegraph); IFRC: "4 confirmed fatalities, over 8,915 affected people, more than 700 damaged or flooded houses"
